decision.explanation: The evidence from pmid-25669829 supports the claim that the combination of Pazopanib and Vorinostat is associated with improved sensitivity/response (specifically longer progression-free survival and overall survival) in patients with sarcoma harboring specific TP53 hotspot mutations. Fragment f01 explicitly mentions that in sarcoma cases (n=3/6), detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R175H and TP53 H193R, which are the specific variants listed in the claim. Fragment f02 provides quantitative data for the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma, showing that those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations had significantly longer median PFS (6.5 months vs 2.0 months) and median OS (19.8 months vs 7.2 months) compared to TP53-undetected cases. This indicates a positive predictive association (sensitivity/response) for the combination therapy in the context of these specific TP53 mutations in sarcoma.

citations.quote: In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation.  In sarcoma cases (n=3/6), detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R175H, TP53 H193R, and TP53 DBDdel (not specified).

In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.
